A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Data Mixing Agent study, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. v1 ends with references; v2 includes Appendices A-F, which retain substantial material moved from v1's main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-pretraining experiments on math and code, start-state estimation experiments, and trajectory and data-efficiency analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds DBL comparisons, computational-cost measurements and checkpoint-level reward-alignment analysis.

M1.justification: The stated CQL loss changes: Equation 5 replaces the log-sum-exp conservative term with an expectation over sampled actions. The trajectory sampler, Transformer architectures, SFT warm-up and inference pipeline remain intact. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an implementation change.

E1.justification: The same source corpora, math and code datasets, 14 downstream benchmarks and synthetic-source/Pythia scenarios are retained. Pythia results move into the appendix. The medical domain is mentioned only as an untested limitation.

E2.justification: v2 adds Dynamic Batch Loading, attributed to Xia et al. (2023), to the 2D math comparisons for three LLaMA models and the LLaMA-DCLM code comparison. Existing comparators remain; DBL is not evaluated in the Pythia or 52D comparisons.

E3.justification: The feedback sets change from 1,531 MMLU and 1,500 MATH examples in v1 Section 3.1 to 500 each in v2 Appendix C.2. v2 also introduces GPU-hour and cross-benchmark variance metrics and a five-checkpoint consistency evaluation. These reported changes do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds computational-efficiency comparisons in Section 4.4 and tests feedback-to-benchmark agreement across five checkpoints in Appendix E.5. The original SFT comparison, trajectory analyses and data-efficiency curves are retained, often relocated or redisplayed.

E5.justification: Appendix E.5 introduces Pearson correlation estimation across five checkpoints, reporting 0.943 for general performance and 0.919 for math. Both versions retain five-run averaging for start-state estimation. The new cross-benchmark variance column measures performance balance, not uncertainty across runs.

E6.justification: All 40 existing math-result rows and 10 code-result rows retain their numerical values. v2 adds DBL results, including overall DCLM scores of 43.50 for math and 43.52 for code, plus GPU hours, benchmark variances and five checkpoint-level feedback/accuracy records in Table 5.

T1.justification: Equation 5 changes the mathematical definition of the conservative penalty from log-sum-exp over action values to expected Q under U(A). This exceeds a notation change. The MDP formulation, SFT objective and reward definition are otherwise retained; no new formal proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain learned domain reweighting, balanced continual-pretraining performance, generalization without retraining and reduced source-data dependence. The new comparator and efficiency measurements principally support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses restricted evaluation coverage, untested applicability to large-scale pretraining and possible failure under substantial field shifts. It also adds model-selection justifications and explains upfront agent-training costs and their reuse across applications.

D1.justification: v2 documents DBL's substituted reference losses and reweighting setup, specifies RegMix's proxy architecture, and discloses 1996.08 GPU hours for trajectory collection and evaluation plus under ten minutes for agent training. Most existing hardware, software and implementation descriptions are relocated rather than newly supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hoffmann et al. (2022) when explaining DBL's scaling-law basis and removes Dyer et al. (2022). It more explicitly positions the comparison against static RegMix and dynamic DBL. Most related-work content is retained in Appendix F.

P1.justification: The main narrative is extensively condensed and reorganized. Algorithms, detailed methodological explanations, experimental settings, full analyses and related work move into appendices. v2 also adds an agent-definition discussion and limitations section and shortens target-model names.

P2.justification: v2 switches to two columns, revises the pipeline illustration and combines selected existing plots into Figure 3 while retaining full plots in appendices. Tables are reorganized into main-text and appendix versions, gain comparator and metric displays, and include the new checkpoint Table 5.

improvement.justification: The dynamic baseline, explicit computational-cost accounting and reward-alignment check address specific evidential gaps in v1. The limitations section also clarifies applicability. These provide a limited net improvement, while unexplained revisions to the CQL objective and feedback-set sizes leave uncertainty about how the retained results relate to the revised method description.
